transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-09-10
Start time: 14:00 UTC
Duration: 47 minutes
Attendees: Alex Martinez (Redwood AE), Jordan Lee (Redwood SE), Casey Nguyen (AriaSearch - Search Eng), Maya Patel (AriaSearch - CTO), Liam O'Connor (AriaSearch - ML Eng)

Auto-generated summary (auto):
- AriaSearch is exploring embedding-based reranking to improve relevance for long-tail queries and to support semantic search across product docs and support tickets.
- Primary constraints: 99th percentile latency target <= 120ms for rerank path, throughput 200 qps at peak, data residency in EU, SOC 2 and KMS requirements.
- Options discussed: Redwood Hosted (fast to try), Dedicated (reserved GPU pools for consistent throughput), Private (VPC/on-prem for strict controls).
- Next steps agreed: share security docs, run a small benchmark, send pricing and pilot plan.

Topics: Embeddings dimensionality, vector DB integration, hybrid search (BM25 + embeddings), throughput and batching, dedicated vs hosted vs private, KMS and audit logs, canary rollout for rerank model.

Transcript body:
[00:00:00] Alex: Hey all, thanks for joining. Quick intros, I'm Alex on the AE side, Jordan's our solutions engineer, and then over to you folks?
[00:00:07] Casey: Hey, Casey here, I run search infra at AriaSearch.
[00:00:09] Maya: Maya, CTO. Nice to meet you.
[00:00:11] Liam: Liam, ML eng, I own the rerank models and embedding experiments.
[00:00:16] Jordan: Great, thanks. Agenda \u2014 understand current infra, goals for embeddings + rerank, constraints, and talk through Redwood options and a pilot.

[00:02:05] Casey: To give context, we're currently on Elastic managed for retrieval and some custom BM25 tweaks. We push a classical ranker plus a small neural reranker for top 50 results but it's slow and costs a lot at scale. We're looking at vector-based candidate retrieval then a learned reranker.
[00:02:38] Liam: Our embeddings currently use a 768-d model from open-source. We're evaluating 1) moving to 1536 dim for better semantic coverage vs 2) quantized 768 to save storage. Need advice on trade offs.
[00:03:12] Jordan: Totally. On dimensionality, higher dims usually give better nearest neighbor separation but cost storage and compute. We often recommend profiling both \u2014 Redwood supports both and you can run the embedding generation elsewhere and push vectors to your vector DB, or use Redwood embeddings for convenience.
[00:03:55] Maya: Data residency is huge \u2014 all customer PII must stay in EU. What are Redwood's options there?
[00:04:10] Alex: Good callout. Hosted has EU regions, we can ensure data at rest in EU and restrict replication. Dedicated gives you isolated GPU pools in region, and Private (VPC) puts control with you \u2014 including bring-your-own KMS. Jordan will share the security pack.

[00:05:30] Casey: How do you typically integrate with vector DBs? We're evaluating Pinecone and Milvus, also looked at Weaviate.
[00:05:42] Jordan: Redwood integrates cleanly with any vector store. Most customers use Redwood to generate embeddings and then ingest into vector DBs for large-scale indexing. For rerank workflows we also offer an end-to-end path where Redwood can serve the reranker model at low latency after vector candidates \u2014 avoids extra network hops. But if you already have a vector DB and want to keep it, we support that.
[00:06:18] Liam: Important for us is hybrid search \u2014 combine BM25 for exact matches plus embeddings for semantic. Any advice on architecture pattern?
[00:06:26] Jordan: Common pattern: run a lightweight lexical candidate set from Elastic (BM25), union with top-K from vector search, then run a learned reranker over concatenated candidates. Redwood's routing can handle multi-stage pipelines and keep traceability for logging. Also prefix/KV caching matters for repeated queries.

[00:08:05] Casey: Performance \u2014 our SLA is fairly tight. We want rerank latency 95th <= 80ms and 99th <= 120ms. At peak we estimate 200 qps with spikes. Can Dedicated meet that?
[00:08:22] Jordan: Dedicated is the most predictable \u2014 reserved GPUs and you can size for QPS. With batching and KV cache, we can push up throughput and keep latency low, but batching sometimes adds tail latency for sparse query patterns. We usually tune batch windows and dynamic batching to hit your p95/SLO.
[00:09:03] Liam: Do you expose batch config or is it managed?
[00:09:08] Jordan: It's configurable \u2014 we give defaults and you can tune. Redwood Optimize can suggest batching thresholds and quantization to balance cost vs latency.

[00:10:00] Maya: Cost question \u2014 Hosted ephemeral GPUs vs Dedicated reserved capacity \u2014 how should we think?
[00:10:09] Alex: Hosted is good for PoC and lowers ops, you pay per-token/ per-inference. Dedicated has commit pricing and is cheaper per-token if you have steady load. Private is higher upfront but necessary for strict controls. We'll send a cost model with examples based on your 200 qps profile.

[00:12:44] Casey: One thing \u2014 our reranker takes a candidate set of 128 and does cross-attention, heavy memory. Can Redwood run cross-attention rerankers efficiently?
[00:12:58] Jordan: Yes, our runtime supports cross-attention optimizations and KV cache management. For heavy cross-attention on 128 candidates we recommend a dedicated instance class or sharded execution. Also consider using a lighter embedding-based dot-product scorer as a first pass and only run cross-attention for final top 10 to save cycles.
[00:13:45] Liam: That could be a good trade. We'll test top-50 vs top-10 rerank.

[00:15:20] Casey: About vector dimensionality \u2014 any rules of thumb for storage and recall?
[00:15:27] Jordan: Roughly, 1536 dims increases storage by ~2x vs 768. ANN search cost also increases; however product docs with many short contexts sometimes benefit from higher dims. Quantization to 8-bit or 4-bit with Redwood's quantization-friendly paths can help. We'll provide quantization profiles for your models.

[00:16:50] Maya: Security \u2014 SSO/ SAML, RBAC, audit logs, KMS. We need to ensure keys never leave our control.
[00:16:58] Alex: For Private we support BYO-KMS and HSM integrations; Dedicated and Hosted support customer-managed keys in EU regions with restricted key policies. Jordan will attach the SOC2 and encryption whitepaper.

[00:18:30] Liam: Latency from region hop matters. If we keep data in EU but traffic originates in NA, what do customers usually do?
[00:18:40] Jordan: We recommend regional routing \u2014 keep inference in the region closest to users or use fallback routing when EU capacity constrained. There's a latency vs data residency tradeoff.

[00:20:10] Casey: Benchmarks \u2014 can we run a dry-run with our dataset? We want a realistic QPS test and a recall/precision comparison vs our current ranker.
[00:20:19] Alex: Absolutely. Typical POC: we spin up a dedicated trial slice or use Hosted with reserved capacity for the benchmark. You provide sample docs and query traces, we run end-to-end throughput + quality tests and share a report.

[00:22:05] Maya: Any gotchas around vector DB consistency? We're concerned about freshness \u2014 support tickets come in every minute.
[00:22:16] Jordan: For high freshness, many teams use a hybrid approach: store recent docs in a fast index and background reindex periodically, or stream updates to vector DB with append-only index. Redwood supports streaming ingestion and can be configured to invalidate cache on writes.

[00:24:30] Casey: Can you talk about function/tool calling or structure outputs? Our reranker outputs need structured signals for the UI.
[00:24:40] Jordan: Redwood supports structured outputs and annotations; the reranker can emit score breakdowns and feature attributions that you can ingest into your UI telemetry. We include per-request traces for rollouts and canary debugging.

[00:26:50] Liam: Competitors \u2014 we've looked at Pinecone for vector storage and their managed rerank flow via external compute. Why choose Redwood over that?
[00:27:01] Alex: Redwood is production-first inference + tooling \u2014 unified runtime across Hosted/Dedicated/Private, model lifecycle controls, and cost optimization tooling. If you want to avoid stitching many services (vector DB + separate inference), Redwood can simplify that while still integrating with your vector DB of choice.

[00:28:44] Casey: Are there any examples of customers doing exactly this hybrid pipeline?
[00:28:50] Jordan: Yes \u2014 we had a retail customer that combined Elastic lexical with vector candidates and Redwood reranker. They cut median time-to-relevant result by 22% and reduced support deflection. I'll share a redacted case study.

[00:30:30] Maya: Rollouts \u2014 we want to A/B test rerank models and be able to roll back quickly.
[00:30:36] Jordan: Redwood Console supports canary deploys, percentage rollouts, and automatic fallback policies if latency or quality regressions occur. You can tie alerts to eval prompt sets too.

[00:33:05] Casey: For the POC, what telemetry will we get? Token-level latency, cost, per-route histograms?
[00:33:12] Alex: Yes \u2014 console shows per-route/model dashboards, per-token cost breakdowns, traces, and error analysis. For POC we'll enable additional logging for your experiment.

[00:35:18] Liam: A question about storage \u2014 if we keep vectors in our DB but cache some prefixes in Redwood, does caching leak data? We need to be careful about PII.
[00:35:29] Jordan: Cache policy is configurable; you can disable prefix/KV cache for sensitive datasets. For Private and Dedicated with stronger isolation options you can maintain stricter controls.

[00:37:40] Casey: Ok, curious on the expected time to get a benchmark running end-to-end.
[00:37:46] Alex: Once you share sample data and query traces, typical timeline is 1 week to run initial throughput/quality benchmarks on Hosted trial; Dedicated trial may take 2 weeks if we provision reserved capacity. We'll put concrete dates in the follow-up.

[00:39:55] Maya: Anything else we should know about model drift monitoring?
[00:40:03] Jordan: Redwood Optimize has quality monitoring and regression alerts tied to prompt sets and evals. We can set up baseline evals and alert on distributional shifts.

[00:42:10] Alex: Quick recap \u2014 we'll send Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private price comparison, SOC2/security pack, a pilot plan and sample case study; you (Casey/Liam) will send sample docs and query traces; schedule a 1-hour benchmark the week of 9/20.
[00:42:30] Casey: Sounds good.
[00:42:33] Liam: We'll get you traces by end of next week.
[00:42:36] Maya: Thanks everyone.
[00:42:40] Alex: Thanks all \u2014 Jordan, you'll share the security docs.
[00:42:45] Jordan: Will do.
[00:42:55] (meeting ends)
